title: Limits and cancellation
description:
Write a work queue that runs async jobs with a concurrency limit and supports cancellation:

```csharp
public static class Worker
{
    public static async Task<int> ProcessAsync<T>(
        IEnumerable<T> items,
        Func<T, CancellationToken, Task> work,
        int maxConcurrency,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

    public static long CountPrimes(int limit)      // primes below limit, using all cores
}
```

- `ProcessAsync` runs `work` for every item with at most `maxConcurrency` at a time and returns how many finished successfully. `maxConcurrency` below 1 throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` at once.
- When the token is cancelled, no new items start, running work receives the cancellation through its token, and `ProcessAsync` throws `OperationCanceledException`.
- If a job throws (not because of cancellation), the remaining items are still processed; at the end `ProcessAsync` throws an `AggregateException` with every such exception.
- `CountPrimes` must give the right answer while splitting the work across threads (use `Parallel.For` or tasks and combine the counts safely).
hints: A `SemaphoreSlim(maxConcurrency)` hands out that many places: `await gate.WaitAsync(token)` before starting a job, and `gate.Release()` in a `finally` when it ends.
For `CountPrimes`, the `Parallel.For` overload with a thread-local total (`localInit`, `body`, `localFinally`) lets each thread count on its own and add its count once with `Interlocked.Add`.
